newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New NZ coalition to cut taxes in 1999/00.
newsitem.headline: New NZ coalition to cut taxes in 1999/00.

text.p: New Zealand's new coalition government said on Wednesday it will cut taxes in 1999/00 and beyond, subject to adequate surpluses and a positive referendum on compulsory superannuation.

"In the event of a positive referendum outcome on the (compulsory superannuation) scheme, those tax cuts would be applied as appropriate to fund the increased contributions," the coalition said in a paper prepared on its fiscal parameters.
Should the compulsory super scheme proceed, contributions would rise in five annual stages from three percent in 1998-99 to eight percent in 2002-3.
"If surpluses remained adequate, taxes would also be cut by two percent in 1999-2000 and one percent in each of the next three years," the paper said.
The second round of the National Party's income tax cut package, which has been legislated for and was due to come into effect on July 1, 1997, has been delayed by 12 months.
